Changes in Chromosome StructureDeletion¨Occurs when an end of a chromosome breaks off, or two simultaneous breaks lead to the loss of an internal segment¨Normally causes abnormalities, even if only in one copy of chromosome
Duplication¨Presence of a chromosome segment more than once in a chromosome¨May or may not result in abnormalities
explanation: This slide describes deletions and duplications, which are structural alterations of chromosomes. A deletion occurs when the end of a chromosome breaks off, or when two simultaneous breaks lead to the loss of an internal segment. Deletions typically cause phenotypic abnormalities, even if they occur in only one copy of the chromosome. A duplication is the presence of a chromosome segment more than once within a chromosome. Unlike deletions, duplications may or may not cause abnormalities depending on the genetic content involved.

questions.q: What is a chromosomal deletion, and what is its typical developmental effect?
opts: The duplication of a chromosome segment; it never causes issues.
The loss of an end piece or internal segment of a chromosome; it normally causes abnormalities even if present in only one copy.
The 180-degree flip of a chromosome; it is always lethal.
The attachment of a chromosome segment to a non-homologous partner; it causes no symptoms.
questions.exp: Option B is correct because the slide defines deletion as occurring when 'an end of a chromosome breaks off, or two simultaneous breaks lead to the loss of an internal segment' and states it 'Normally causes abnormalities, even if only in one copy of chromosome.'

questions.q: What is a chromosomal duplication as defined on the slide?
opts: The presence of a chromosome segment more than once in a chromosome.
The loss of an internal segment of DNA.
The movement of a segment to a different chromosome.
questions.exp: Option A is correct because the slide defines duplication as: 'Presence of a chromosome segment more than once in a chromosome.'
